name: PATN2 (a second leopard-complex modifier, not published)
summary: A made-up stand-in for the rest of what shapes a leopard-complex pattern. Only two loci are published: LP itself (TRPM1) and PATN1 (RFWD3). UC Davis says other genes help set how much white an LP horse has, so more modifiers are inferred, but none has been mapped, no variant or test exists, and no source names a PATN2 - it may be one undiscovered gene, several small ones, or polygenic background. Here, on an LP horse it gives the blanket patterns - a white sheet over the hips, spotted or not - and with PATN1 the semi-leopard between the two; that split is this data's model. The old idea that a PATN2 is the blanket gene has been given up, and PATN1 itself sets the amount of white rather than a leopard or blanket shape. Invisible on a horse without LP; no known effect on health or build.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Carried, but silent on its own - it only shapes the pattern of a horse that also carries the leopard complex.
